findings.reason: The protected solution is minimal, conventional, and interview-ready. The direct set name makes the deliberately non-transitive relation explicit, left/right identify declared pairs, and first/second identify aligned sentence words; the early length guard and final all expression contain no unnecessary machinery.

Equal sentence lengths establish a one-to-one positional comparison. Inserting each declared pair in both orientations implements symmetry exactly, while direct set membership performs no graph traversal and therefore does not introduce forbidden transitive relationships. At each aligned position, string equality supplies reflexive similarity and membership supplies explicit pair similarity. The universal check returns true exactly when every position satisfies one of those permitted conditions.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 734, Python, and the native areSentencesSimilar(sentence1, sentence2, similarPairs) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms nonempty one-to-1000-word sentence arrays, one-to-20-character English-letter words, zero-to-1000 distinct two-word pairs, equal-length necessity, aligned comparison, reflexive equality, symmetric direct pairs, deliberately non-transitive similarity, and the Boolean sentence result.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065812494 are algorithmically identical: both use the same length rejection, bidirectional pair-set construction, aligned equality-or-membership test, and all-position result. Their only structural differences are the required Solution.areSentencesSimilar wrapper and Python typing dialect.

The unchanged three authored workloads grow n + p from 8 to 112 with every aligned word requiring a direct pair and the pair list ordered opposite the sentence positions. In a fresh real-test run, the exact protected source passed all twelve visible correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent -0.01 and a 1.03x largest runtime ratio. A correct control that scans all declared pairs for each alignment matched every output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +0.70, distinguishing expected O(n+p) hash preprocessing from quadratic repeated lookup on this family.

The Approach accurately derives the length guard, symmetric direct-pair set, aligned equality and membership checks, and intentional absence of transitive closure. Its expected O(n+p) time and O(p) auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The modular Reference preserves the source's sentence-to-array illustration, declared direct-pair model, Boolean objective, two positional similarity conditions, reflexive rule, and non-transitivity warning. It includes all three exact source examples with independently worded explanations, all eight constraints, and the source-native direct-pair hint.

Authenticated Premium source review verified exactly three explained examples, two definition bullets, eight constraints, no images or tables, and one provider hint. source_fidelity.json binds the live statement hash eb97ff07e599c86400a234b7d478ba96ff6672fa86e4f2ee56eaba8cce4c21f5 and every composed Reference section; the independent validator reports verified with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly three examples. Their exact sentence arrays, pair lists, outputs, and explanation facts now appear first in source order; the former invented non-transitive sample was retained as a visible trial instead of being represented as source Example 3.

All twelve ordinary correctness checks are visible samples or trials. The former hidden missing-pair, repeated-word, unused-pair, and all-reversed-orientation behaviors were exposed, while the duplicate pair that violated the source's distinct-pair guarantee was removed.

Contract boundaries cover one-word sentences, an empty pair list, one-character words, mixed upper/lower case, and exact twenty-character sentence and pair words in authored cases. Separate generated checks jointly exercise 1000-word sentences and 1000 distinct pairs, plus a 1000-versus-999 length mismatch.

Material behavior covers reflexive equality, symmetric orientation, direct pairs at every alignment, one word with several direct neighbors, repeated sentence words, unused declared pairs, one missing alignment, empty-pair failure, sentence-length rejection, case sensitivity, and the semantic trap that similarity is not transitive.

Expected results were checked against an independent direct-pair-scan oracle for all fifteen authored correctness-plus-benchmark inputs, 12168 exhaustive sentence/relation combinations, 5000 deterministic random legal relations, and maximum-count boundaries. The protected app adapter and immutable native Solution agreed throughout.

The unchanged 8, 32, and 112-unit workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, span 14x, and make the correct repeated-pair-scan control fail only the scaling verdict; the latest run measured relative growth exponent +0.70 for that control.
